gaps.sentence: City rents are crippling. In the countryside, ___, property is far cheaper.
gaps.explanation: 'On the other hand' moves to a contrasting (not opposite) situation.

gaps.sentence: ___ the fact that costs had doubled, the project was allowed to continue.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite the fact that' = although, in a more formal wrapper.

gaps.sentence: I enjoyed the film; the ending was weak, ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Though' can come at the end of a sentence as a casual contrast marker; the others cannot.

gaps.sentence: My sister is terribly reserved, ___ I'll talk to complete strangers.
gaps.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two parallel facts: her nature versus mine.

gaps.sentence: ___ the price, the location is absolutely perfect.
gaps.explanation: 'Apart from the price' = the only negative in an otherwise positive description.

gaps.sentence: He is far from lazy; ___, he trains six hours a day.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' rejects the description and states the reverse, more strongly.

gaps.sentence: Insure the camera ___ it gets damaged in transit.
gaps.explanation: 'In case it gets damaged' = as a precaution against damage.

gaps.sentence: I know exactly what the risks are. ___, I'm going anyway.
gaps.hint: doing it in spite of risk
